mission: AISA works with multilateral bodies and national institutions across Asia to strengthen AI governance, acting as a bridge between technical frontier risks and national policy. It argues Asia's 'middle powers' have leverage over AI's infrastructure and should use it together, and runs diplomacy simulations, civil-society training and AI-biosecurity work.

key_work.title: AI Diplomacy Crisis tabletop exercises (Geneva and APEC)
key_work.plain_summary: Simulated AI crises for deputy ministers, UN ambassadors and diplomats, including on the official APEC agenda, to practise international responses.

key_work.title: Asia roundtables on AI safety (Jakarta, Manila, Singapore, Beijing, Seoul, Tokyo)
key_work.plain_summary: A series of regional roundtables on Asia's perspective on AI risks and preparedness, published on its YouTube channel.

warnings.text: Frontier AI is being built and governed by a handful of dominant actors while most nations negotiate with them alone.
AI governance terms may be 'locked in' before Asian countries have a say.
AI-enabled biological risks are emerging in the region.

recommendations.text: Asian middle powers should coordinate and use their collective leverage over AI infrastructure.
Build regional networks steering AI toward public accountability, plurality and human flourishing.
Train civil society and diplomats to handle AI crises.
